subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: Tolman's rats, after exploring a maze freely, could take efficient shortcuts to the goal box even along paths never directly reinforced before, suggesting rats form:

options.option_text: An internal cognitive map of the maze's layout
No mental representation of any kind

explanation: Tolman argued that rats build cognitive maps — mental representations of spatial layout — enabling flexible, efficient navigation beyond simple reinforced stimulus-response habits.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch7 — Learning Theories
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: Skinner's principle of shaping, when applied to instructional design, led to the development of:

options.option_text: Programmed instruction with small steps and immediate feedback
Whole-class lecturing with no individual pacing
Pure discovery learning with zero teacher guidance
Corporal punishment as the primary teaching tool

explanation: Skinner translated operant principles into programmed instruction — small graded steps with active responding and immediate reinforcement, an early precursor to today's adaptive learning software.
